title: 08. Multi-Agent & Patterns: RAG Metrics
summary: What is RAG evaluation? > Evaluating the entire pipeline: retrieve documents → generate answer. > 3 components: Retrieval quality + Context quality + Generation quality

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
> **What is RAG evaluation?**
> Evaluating the entire pipeline: retrieve documents → generate answer.
> 3 components: Retrieval quality + Context quality + Generation quality

sections.title: The RAG Evaluation Triangle
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    RAG EVALUATION TRIANGLE                      │
│                                                                 │
│                        QUESTION                                 │
│                            │                                    │
│                  ┌─────────┼─────────┐                          │
│                  │                   │                          │
│                  ▼                   ▼                          │
│             CONTEXT               ANSWER                        │
│          (Retrieved)           (Generated)                      │
│                  │                   │                          │
│                  └─────────┬─────────┘                          │
│                            │                                    │
│  3 RELATIONSHIPS TO MEASURE:                                    │
│                                                                 │
│  1. Question ↔ Context  = CONTEXT RELEVANCE                    │
│     "Did we retrieve the right docs for this question?"        │
│                                                                 │
│  2. Context  ↔ Answer   = FAITHFULNESS                         │
│     "Is the answer actually based on the retrieved docs?"      │
│                                                                 │
│  3. Question ↔ Answer   = ANSWER RELEVANCE                     │
│     "Does the answer actually address the question?"           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Faithfulness
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  FAITHFULNESS = "Is EVERY claim in the answer supported        │
│                  by the retrieved context?"                     │
│                                                                 │
│  This is the ANTI-HALLUCINATION metric.                        │
│  1.0 = fully grounded   0.0 = pure hallucination               │
│                                                                 │
│  HOW IT'S MEASURED:                                            │
│  Step 1: Extract all claims from the answer                    │
│  Step 2: Check each claim against the context                  │
│  Step 3: Score = supported claims / total claims               │
│                                                                 │
│  EXAMPLE:                                                       │
│  Context: "LangChain was created in October 2022 by Harrison   │
│            Chase. It supports Python and JavaScript."           │
│                                                                 │
│  Answer: "LangChain was created in 2022 by Harrison Chase.     │
│           It supports Python, JavaScript, and Java."            │
│                                                                 │
│  Claims extracted:                                              │
│  ✅ "created in 2022"         → in context                     │
│  ✅ "by Harrison Chase"       → in context                     │
│  ✅ "supports Python"         → in context                     │
│  ✅ "supports JavaScript"     → in context                     │
│  ❌ "supports Java"           → NOT in context! HALLUCINATION  │
│                                                                 │
│  Faithfulness = 4 supported / 5 total = 0.80                   │
│                                                                 │
│  ✅ Good:  0.90+   ⚠️  OK: 0.75    ❌ Bad: 0.60-              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Answer Relevance
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ANSWER RELEVANCE = "Does the answer actually ANSWER           │
│                      the question asked?"                       │
│                                                                 │
│  This catches answers that are correct but OFF-TOPIC.          │
│                                                                 │
│  EXAMPLES:                                                      │
│                                                                 │
│  Question: "What is the capital of France?"                    │
│                                                                 │
│  Answer A: "Paris is the capital of France."                   │
│  → Answer Relevance: 1.00 ✅ Directly answers the question     │
│                                                                 │
│  Answer B: "France is a country in Western Europe with         │
│             a population of 68 million people."                 │
│  → Answer Relevance: 0.20 ❌ About France but misses question  │
│                                                                 │
│  Answer C: "Paris is the capital of France. It was            │
│             established as the capital in the 10th century."   │
│  → Answer Relevance: 0.90 ✅ Answers + adds relevant context  │
│                                                                 │
│  TRICK: An answer can be FAITHFUL (grounded in context) but    │
│  have LOW RELEVANCE (doesn't answer the actual question).      │
│  You need BOTH metrics!                                         │
│                                                                 │
│  ✅ Good:  0.85+   ⚠️  OK: 0.70    ❌ Bad: 0.50-              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Context Relevance
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  CONTEXT RELEVANCE = "Are the retrieved documents actually     │
│                       useful for answering the question?"       │
│                                                                 │
│  This evaluates your RETRIEVER quality from the RAG side.      │
│                                                                 │
│  HOW IT'S MEASURED:                                            │
│  Count sentences in context that are relevant to the question  │
│  Score = relevant sentences / total sentences                  │
│                                                                 │
│  EXAMPLE:                                                       │
│  Question: "How does NDCG work?"                               │
│                                                                 │
│  Retrieved Context (5 sentences):                              │
│  ✅ "NDCG measures ranking quality using discounted gains"     │
│  ✅ "DCG = Σ relevance(i) / log2(rank+1)"                      │
│  ❌ "Precision@K measures what fraction of results are relevant"│
│  ❌ "The weather in Paris is usually mild in spring"           │
│  ✅ "NDCG normalizes DCG by the ideal DCG (IDCG)"             │
│                                                                 │
│  Context Relevance = 3/5 = 0.60                                 │
│                                                                 │
│  LOW context relevance means:                                   │
│  → Retriever is pulling noisy/irrelevant documents              │
│  → LLM gets confused with irrelevant context                   │
│  → Higher chance of wrong or hallucinated answers              │
│                                                                 │
│  ✅ Good:  0.80+   ⚠️  OK: 0.60    ❌ Bad: 0.40-              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Token F1, ROUGE-L, Exact Match
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  REFERENCE-BASED METRICS — Compare answer vs ground truth      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  TOKEN F1
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Breaks both answer and ground truth into individual tokens.
  Measures how many tokens OVERLAP.

  Ground Truth: "RAG combines retrieval and generation"
  Predicted:    "RAG uses retrieval augmented generation"

  GT tokens:   {rag, combines, retrieval, and, generation}
  Pred tokens: {rag, uses, retrieval, augmented, generation}
  Common:      {rag, retrieval, generation}  → 3 tokens

  Precision = 3/5 = 0.60   "How much of prediction is correct?"
  Recall    = 3/5 = 0.60   "How much of GT is covered?"
  F1        = 0.60          Harmonic mean

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ROUGE-L (Longest Common Subsequence)
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Finds the LONGEST sequence of words that appear in BOTH
  strings in the SAME ORDER (not necessarily consecutive).

  Ground Truth: "the cat sat on the mat"
  Prediction:   "the cat sat near the mat"
                 ─── ─── ─── ─────── ───
                  ✅  ✅  ✅         ✅  ✅  (LCS = 5)

  ROUGE-L = LCS / max(len(GT), len(Pred)) = 5/6 = 0.83

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  EXACT MATCH
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Binary: 1.0 if strings match exactly, 0.0 otherwise.
  Used for factoid QA where one exact answer is expected.

  Question:     "What year was Python created?"
  Ground Truth: "1991"
  Answer A:     "1991"   → Exact Match = 1.0 ✅
  Answer B:     "Python was created in 1991"  → EM = 0.0 ❌
                (normalized → "python was created in 1991" ≠ "1991")

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  WHICH ONE TO USE?                                              │
│                                                                 │
│  Exact Match → Short factoid answers ("Who is CEO of OpenAI?") │
│  Token F1    → Partial credit for close answers                │
│  ROUGE-L     → Sentence-level similarity, summaries            │
│  LLM Judge   → Open-ended, nuanced answers                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Complete RAG Scorecard
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    RAG SCORECARD EXAMPLE                        │
│                                                                 │
│  Question:    "What is LangGraph?"                              │
│  Ground Truth:"LangGraph is a library for building stateful    │
│                multi-agent workflows using graphs."             │
│  Context:     [doc about LangGraph, doc about LangChain]        │
│  Answer:      "LangGraph enables stateful graph-based agent    │
│                workflows with nodes and edges."                 │
│                                                                 │
│  ┌────────────────────────┬──────────┬───────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Metric                │  Score   │  Verdict              │ │
│  ├────────────────────────┼──────────┼───────────────────────┤ │
│  │  Faithfulness          │  0.95    │  ✅ No hallucination  │ │
│  │  Answer Relevance      │  0.90    │  ✅ On-topic          │ │
│  │  Context Relevance     │  0.85    │  ✅ Good retrieval    │ │
│  │  Correctness           │  0.88    │  ✅ Factually right   │ │
│  │  Completeness          │  0.70    │  ⚠️  Missing details  │ │
│  │  Token F1              │  0.62    │  ⚠️  Different words  │ │
│  │  ROUGE-L               │  0.55    │  ⚠️  Less overlap     │ │
│  │  Exact Match           │  0.00    │  ❌ Not exact (OK!)   │ │
│  ├────────────────────────┼──────────┼───────────────────────┤ │
│  │  OVERALL (weighted)    │  0.83    │  ✅ PASS              │ │
│  └────────────────────────┴──────────┴───────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                 │
│  Insight: Low Exact Match is FINE for open-ended questions.    │
│           High Faithfulness + Relevance = good RAG system.     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
